questions.learningObjective: evaluate weight and optical size in a design critique
questions.stem: On Weight and optical size: a designer reviewing a museum exhibition poster notices that a headline set in a very light weight almost disappears. Which change most directly fixes its visibility?

options.text: Increase the weight so the strokes carry more contrast against the ground
Reduce the tracking until the letters nearly touch one another
options.misconception: mistakes letter spacing for the thickness of the strokes

options.text: Switch to a condensed width while keeping the same light weight
options.misconception: confuses the width of letters with their weight

options.text: Add more leading between the headline and the body text below
options.misconception: blames line spacing for strokes that are simply too thin

questions.explanation: Weight controls stroke thickness, and thicker strokes give a headline more presence and contrast against its background. If a light weight disappears, increasing the weight addresses the visibility directly, unlike changes to spacing or to the width of the letters.

questions.stem: Regarding Kerning pairs: a designer reviewing a fashion lookbook page notices that the letters A and V in a headline leave an awkward gap. What adjustment specifically fixes this problem?

options.text: Reduce the space between that particular pair of letters
Reduce the spacing between every letter in the word uniformly
options.misconception: confuses tracking across a whole word with kerning one pair

options.text: Increase the leading of the entire line of the headline
options.misconception: mistakes vertical line spacing for a horizontal gap

options.text: Change the color of the two letters to draw attention away
options.misconception: substitutes emphasis for actually correcting a spacing fault

questions.explanation: Kerning adjusts the spacing between a specific pair of letters to even out the visual gap created by their shapes, such as the open wedge of an A beside a V. Reducing the space for that pair fixes the problem without altering the spacing of the whole word.
questions.hint: Does the problem affect one pair of letters or every letter?
